hints: Differentiate $\sin y\ln x=x-2\sin y$ implicitly, treating $y$ as a function of $x$.
Use the product rule on $\sin y\ln x$: its derivative contains both $\cos y\,dy/dx$ and $1/x$.
Collect every term containing $dy/dx$ on one side.
Factor out and isolate $dy/dx$ in terms of $x$ and $y$.
walkthrough:
Write the given curve equation:
$$\sin y\ln x = x - 2\sin y$$

Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$ using implicit differentiation and the product rule on the left-hand side:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(\sin y\ln x) = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x - 2\sin y)$$

Compute each derivative term, using the chain rule on $\sin y$:
$$\left(\cos y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right)\ln x + \sin y\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = 1 - 2\cos y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$

Collect all terms containing $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ on the left-hand side and remaining terms on the right-hand side:
$$\cos y\ln x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} + 2\cos y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1 - \dfrac{\sin y}{x}$$

Factor out $\cos y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ on the left-hand side:
$$(\ln x + 2)\cos y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1 - \dfrac{\sin y}{x}$$

Divide both sides by $(\ln x + 2)\cos y$ to isolate $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{\sin y}{x}}{(\ln x + 2)\cos y} = \dfrac{x - \sin y}{x(\ln x + 2)\cos y}$$

hints: A tangent parallel to the $x$-axis has $dy/dx=0$, so set the numerator from part (i) equal to zero.
Use $1-\sin y/x=0$ to express $\sin y$ in terms of $x$.
Substitute this relation into $\sin y(\ln x+2)=x$ and solve the resulting equation in $\ln x$.
walkthrough: A tangent parallel to the $x$-axis has gradient $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$.

Set the numerator of $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ equal to zero:
$$1 - \dfrac{\sin y}{x} = 0 \implies \dfrac{\sin y}{x} = 1 \implies \sin y = x$$

Substitute $\sin y = x$ into the original equation of the curve $\sin y\ln x = x - 2\sin y$:
$$x\ln x = x - 2x$$
$$x\ln x = -x$$

Since $\ln x$ requires $x > 0$, divide both sides by $x$:
$$\ln x = -1$$

Solve for $x$ by exponentiating both sides:
$$x = \mathrm{e}^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{e}}$$
